dishes.name: Boyoz
dishes.desc: Flaky, oily pastry brought by Sephardic Jews, eaten on weekend mornings with a boiled egg. Found almost only in İzmir.

dishes.name: İzmir lokma
dishes.desc: Small fried dough balls soaked in syrup, sold warm from shops and carts. The İzmir version is crisp outside and syrupy inside.

dishes.name: Şambali
dishes.desc: Semolina cake soaked in syrup and topped with almond or cream, a dessert strongly linked to İzmir.

dishes.name: Kumru
dishes.desc: Toasted roll filled with sucuk, tomato and cheese. Born in Çeşme on the Aegean coast and now eaten all over İzmir.

dishes.name: Aegean wild greens
dishes.desc: Boiled wild herbs dressed with olive oil and lemon, a staple of Aegean meyhanes and the kitchens of Çeşme and Urla.

dishes.name: İzmir tulum cheese
dishes.desc: Crumbly, salty goat's-milk cheese ripened in a skin, made in the İzmir hills and served at breakfast.
